3 different screens when you are checking your irregular heartbeat is too many, possibly very dangerous if you are checking to see if you are having real heart issues. The 3 screens (an Ad for more services), the screen of what you would like to do (record services), "which EKG device you are using 3 lead or 6, then touch to your leg.

When you open the Omron Heart Rate Monitor and press the sync button it works with the 1st screen and syncs automatically with Kardia. Why can't Kardia?

It would be great if when you opened the App and clicked the first screen you were able to take your EKG right away or at least make it as a device option for those of us that bought this due to major health issues.  Many of us are using this as a real time solution for irregular heart beat monitoring that the DR cannot catch with a conventional 24hr wearable Med device.

Ah Lastly it also asks you if you would like to upgrade to storing your results online with no way to upgrade, it doesn't upgrade.

text_fidelity_a:
Aerobie Superdisc (6044022) My Black Lab can't get enough Frisbee, she demands it at least twice a day. Unlike the flying discs made specifically for dogs, these fly just like a real Frisbee (both in distance and flight pattern) yet have the soft rim so the dog"s mouth isn't injured when she catches it in mid-air. The brightly colored rim makes them easy to find when my throwing gets too wild and they end up somewhere she can't get to. The rim is squared off and ever so slightly raised above the actual disc which makes it easier for her to pick up if it lands flat on a slick or level surface.

I have tried many versions of Frisbees through the last 40 years of Labs in my life and these are by far the best. The one I just had to throw out was over 5 years old and eventually cracked in half but up until then flew perfectly despite being riddled with teeth marks, dents, and small cracks.

The size makes them unsuitable for small dogs (obviously) and because the rim is the only color they may be difficult for dogs (and humans) with imperfect eyesight to see.

text_fidelity_a:
Zippo HeatBank 9s Plus Rechargeable Hand Warmer All of the Zippo hand warmers are offered on this listing. Though some of them look similar, they are not all the same. The one that I have is the 9-Hour Plus model. Make sure you are reading the review for the hand warmer you are interested in.

This device, being produced by Zippo, historically a lighter manufacturer, has the look and feel of a large cigarette lighter. Even the power button is located for thumb operation and is configured much like you’d use a lighter. That’s kind of cool, actually. The feel in the hand is very nice and comfortable. When the power button is depressed for 3+ seconds, the heater comes on at level 1, side one. There are six total heat levels that involve levels one through three, single sided of the unit, and one through three with both sides heating. I can tell you that I was totally amazed at how quickly the unit heated up. Almost instantly you feel significant heat. It cools back down almost as quickly. While the unit does not have a pouch with it, like some similar devices of other brands, I’d consider that it’s not likely to burn you unless you kept it on the high setting right against the skin for a significant amount of time. However, I would not consider this a device for young children. The detachable lanyard, which does not show in the pictures, was a stroke of genius! It measures 18 inches long. You can wear it around your neck at, say, a sporting event that you’d be at for a while in cool temperatures, and be able to detach the device from the lanyard with the latch, turn it on and put in a pocket or pass it to a friend, and then attach it again. Just a great convenience. And, of course, the fact that it has two ports for charging external devices. It only comes with one short charging cord however, the Micro USB that it takes to charge the device itself. Of course you could use it to charge a compatible Micro USB device. IOS users will have to furnish a cord. I just really like this device and find it very useful. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Zippo HeatBank 9s Plus Rechargeable Hand Warmer

Therefore, we have not yet been on the water to use these. We are also beginners at doing and owning these, so please consider this when reading). I’ve always preferred kayaking over SUPing, mainly because having spent my life into my 30s playing sports, the ankles have taken a number of hits and at this point, can get sore quickly - SUPing involves a lot of wear and tear on the ankles. So I have looked at inflatable kayaks, not finding anything I think is of a quality that matches inflatable SUPs. And to that end, my wife and I have gotten inflatable SUPs instead. But, I also knew that I could use the inflatable SUP as a kayak on its own, but if I added this Apurioni Kayak Seat with Back Support Adjustable Straps and Deluxe Padded Cushion it would give me some of the same support as a kayak seat. In the end, I am very glad I grabbed this Apurioni Kayak Seat. This is actually the second of two such seats, so both of us can use a seat on our SUP. This Apurioni Kayak Seat seems to be well designed, with good, solid construction, and good materials. There were no instructions and we’d not used such things before, so it came to common sense to put together and that was easy enough. The seat attaches by 4 hooks to the SUP’s D Rings on the surface. You adjust the tension of the straps to make sure it’s secure and at a good position, and in doing so, once seated, it holds the seat in place. Both of us tried this Apurioni Kayak Seat and found it comfortable. It is not meant to be the same kind of chair you sit on in your living room, but we both found this gives one support to help “support” sitting for a longer period of time. We have not taken it out, so I don’t know the longevity - I’ll come back and update if I have any issues once we can get out there - but for now, it seems like it’ll be a great support on a SUP trip. The material also seems like it’ll hold up fine to salt water, but we plan to wash it every use with fresh water post-use. There is a detachable bag on the bag, connected by clips, allowing you to carry things with (like water - tight bag for your gear - that would go inside this non-water proof bag, and can be detached so you can carry it separately. In the end, this seems like it’s going to be a good seat for our needs and we can’t wait to get out there and use it!
text_fidelity_b: Apurioni Kayak Seat with Back Support Adjustable Straps and Deluxe Padded Cushion with Waterproof Storage Bag

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can put things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

I could have picked any of the NCAA teams that they make this cooler for, but I happened to pick the colors of my favorite pro football team, the Pittsburgh Steelers. text_fidelity_a:
Nalgene OTF On-The-Fly Water Bottle - 24 fl. oz. (710 ml) I live an on-the-go kind of life. I'm always running from point A to point B with a big tote or a backpack full of things that cannot get water damage. I've used dozens of water bottles over the years and there's always been a problem: one is too big so it doesn't fit in my purse or water bottle pocket on my backpack, another leaks like nobody's business, another has a straw that just won't stay attached so you're sipping air most of the time, and others just don't lock up nice and tight.

One day, I was talking with my sister over lunch and I had noticed she pulled this water bottle from the dark recesses of her tote and nothing in her purse was wet. I was impressed. She had gotten this water bottle when she bought a 4 years ago and had used this water bottle exclusively since. She took it with her abroad and takes it to college classes everyday with no problems. After I hear her rave reviews, I decided to buy one.

I've been using this water bottle for a few months now and I honestly am in love. The slim design makes it unique compared to the typical Nalgene but it still feels very sturdy. Not quite a liter of water but it's more than the typically grocery story water bottle. The loop on the top makes it easy to grab on the go and even hook, via carabiner, to a strap or your bag. My favorite feature is the locking mouth piece.

In order to drink water, you have to flip the metal lock down and push the button to pop the lid off. I've read some reviews saying that this is too much effort but honestly, I love it. I know that the water bottle won't leak and it hasn't. I work in a school and I carry this around all day. Sometimes my students accidentally kick it across the floor and no water ever leaks. I also drop this bag into my gym bag and nothing gets damp ever. The small mouth piece also makes it great to grab a quick gulp of water while you're in the middle of a run. No twisting off lids: just flip the lock down, press the button and delicious H2O is delivered to your mouth with no spills.

Bottom line: buy this water bottle. I love it and I think you will too.
text_fidelity_b: Nalgene OTF On-The-Fly Water Bottle - 24 fl. oz. (710 ml)

text_fidelity_a:
Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe I've had my safe for a couple weeks now and I am pretty happy with it. I was looking for an inexpensive safe to keep valuables away from the casual thief. This safe is not going to stop a professional thief. For that type of safe you need to pay upwards of $500. This safe is also not fire or waterproof so if you need those types of features look elsewhere.

The safe weighs about 40 pounds so it is critical to bolt it down, otherwise a thief can just walk off with it. There are 4 holes in the back of the safe and 4 holes in the bottom. There were 4 pretty hefty screws provided, I mounted my safe inside a large cabinet and it seems pretty secure. The safe and door are made of pretty heavy gauge steel so it is not going to be easy to just pry it open.

Inside the safe there are two metal shelves held in place by cheap plastic fasteners. But I will get into that later. Programming the security code was very easy and I had no problem opening and closing the safe. The safe also comes with two keys in case you forget your code or if the batteries die. There is a pretty loud beep when the buttons are pressed but that can be turned off.

I just have two minor issues with the safe. First, the cheap plastic fasteners used to hold the shelves in place are useless. When I opened the safe they were laying in the bottom of the safe with the shelves and half of them were broken. Easily resolved though, I just used metal bolts and screws I had to hold the shelves in place. I think manufacturer should provide these. The second issue I had was with the cheap shelf liners provided. They are very thin foam material and don't stay in place when sliding things in and out. Again though easily resolved by replacing with more substantial liner.

Overall I am pretty happy with this safe. I looked at others in the price range and many seemed to have significant quality issues. The issues I have with this safe are very minor and to be expected for a safe at this price point. This safe is a good value for your money as long as you are just looking to protect valuables from a casual thief
text_fidelity_b: Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe

text_fidelity_a:
FYGL Smart Weighted Hula Hoop for Adults Exercise, Weight Loss Fitness Hoop, 2 in 1 Abdomen Fitness Massage Hoops, Great for Beginner Home Workout, 16 Detachable Knots 42 Inches (Winsome Orchid) I’ve tried two of these smart hoops and so far I like the concept more than the product itself, but this does serve a purpose.

First off, this one is smaller than the other I tried, so note the size if you’re on the larger side. I’m a women’s xl and it fits me with maybe 2 pieces out, so if you’re much larger than an xl or carry all of your weight in your waist, you may need extra pieces than are included.

The motion actually feels pretty good. I can waist hoop just fine, but there’s a slightly different feel with this. It’s almost a waist massage. You feel the weight in a very different way from a standard weighted hoop as the weight isn’t constantly going back hit the smacking into your waist. I know people who have found themselves bruised from a standard weighted hoop, that shouldn’t happen with this.

The downside is that these are pretty loud. I’m rather sensitive to sounds and with the hubs still working from home, I cannot do this at the front of the house without disrupting his meetings in the back of the house. Not super overpowering at that distance, but still loud enough to be an annoying clicking back there.

If they were quieter I’d love them. As this hoop is, I like it but not nearly as much as my standard, not weighted, adult sized hula hoop.

I don’t think the screen adds much to this one over the cheaper smart hoop I have without a screen, in fact I don’t bother turning it on, I just use my usual fitness tracker to tell me how I did, it may not tell you how many turns you did like this screen is meant to, but the fitness tracker is getting my heart rate and feels like a more personal / accurate account of what a hooping session did for me.

Overall, I think a standard hoop is better. But this is nice for a change, for those who cannot keep a hoop going (be sure you’re trying with a large adult hoop and not a kids toy store one), for those who want a weighted hoop but who bruise easily, and for those like who like repetitive sounds as they exercise.
text_fidelity_b: FYGL Smart Weighted Hula Hoop for Adults Exercise, Weight Loss Fitness Hoop, 2 in 1 Abdomen Fitness Massage Hoops, Great for Beginner Home Workout, 16 Detachable Knots 42 Inches (Winsome Orchid)

text_fidelity_a: Sawyer Products SP105 MINI Water Filtration System, Single, Black How can a typical backpacker or survivalist review this?  I cannot analyze water before and after through a chemical analysis.  I have to operate a bit on trust and  on taste.  The technology has been evaluated by labs over the years.  So I have tested these according to a 'taste test.'  I do not taste the water purifying compound our fine municipal service uses for our daily water supply.  Brewed coffee tastes 'just that little bit better' when I filtered the water.  I read that Sawyer products are used in serious 'Third World' situations, so I think we will be 'good to go' in the 'Wilds' of Charlottesville, VA or the Great Smokey Mountains or the Blue Ridge Mountains.  I like the standard 'bottle' neck size on these:  I can swap out the small squeeze bag for a larger, empty energy drink bottle.  The straw option that fits on the filter inflow permits sucking up water from pools in shallow streams.  The set comes with a syringe-style backflow flusher to clean the filter of debris.

Viper Dead-On Tournament Bristle Steel Tip Dartboard Set with Staple-Free Bullseye, Metal Triangular Spider Wire for Reduced Bounce Outs and Increased Scoring; High-Grade Self-Healing Sisal Board The dead-on viper sisal fiber dartboard is a classic dartboard that you will likely see in your local bar or pub. The spider, or the metal that separates the segments (numbers and colors), is angled on each side. Therefore, if a dart barely hits the side of the spider then it will be directed to hit the sisal fibers. The angled spider helps reduce the number of bounce backs. However, you should notice that the spider has "staples" that go over the metal bar on both sides. If you do not like this aspect of the dartboard then you can spend an extra $10-$15 bucks and upgrade to the viper spider dartboard. Either board is a great addition to your home game room or man (or woman) cave. Great board. Made in Taiwan.

text_fidelity_a: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo) Let me start by saying that I researched literally dozens of fanny packs before settling on this one. Badlands,Fieldline, LL Bean, ALPS, Allen, Timberhawk, Browning, Cabelas .  .  . you get the picture. I use a fanny pack primarily to run and gun longbeards and to get my archery gear into my hunting locations with a Summit Open Shot Climber on my back. This pack replaces an old fleece 380 cubic inch Fieldline that served me well for many years, but was always just a tad too small.  I can tell you that there are a limited number of packs available that are between what I consider to be too small at 450-500 cubic inches, and for me, too large at over 1000 cubic inches. I don't carry enough gear to require backpack type straps, nor do I want the complications associated with them. Furthermore, many  of the packs that DO tend to fall inside this capacity range  have what I call a "hopper" style zippered opening, which to me makes absolutely no sense. You unzip it and your gear rolls out. I want a top loading pack that retains my gear. If I've just climbed 20' , gotten settled in, unzip my pack and all my gear falls to the ground, well, lets just say I'm not a happy camper. This is a nicely designed pack that met the majority of my parameters developed over 40 years of hunting. This pack, in my opinion, is the perfect size. Enough room for all my gadgets and grub. The side straps "fold" easily and stay "folded" for  easy placement at the back of my platform. Lashing straps top and bottom, check. Plenty of zippered organizing compartments, check. Side strap pockets that actually have some capacity, check.  Oh. . Did I mention this is a great looking pack?  Which leads us to one of my few negatives. The attractive green panels that you see on the front and top of the pack as well as  the entire pack bottom are Dyneema, a super strong synthetic fiber material. Noisy??  Not terribly. Tenzing claims these panels are used for durability, and while I'm fairly certain this pack will indeed outlive my remaining years in the field, they are . . well . . synthetic.  While in my application it means little, if I were using this pack primarily  to stalk or still hunt, it might impact my choice. Get one in your hands and see for yourself. Sizing issue: The reviewer that  mentioned this not cinching up to his 34 waist is spot on. The side straps, at least on the pack i was shipped, are simply too long. I am a 35 waist and can JUST get this pack tight enough. Overall I am extremely happy with the design, build quality, and my Amazon purchase. Nicely done Tenzing.
text_fidelity_b: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo)

I also bought a large package of the Energizer MAX alkaline batteries. The manual recommends using rechargeable batteries and I will probably do that later - as this camera can run down batteries fairly quickly.

I did have some issues with the camera - number one, there was a problem with the strap/buckle that lets you strap the camera to a tree or post. Nothing major - the stitching came loose. I was still able to make it work though and will probably replace the strap when I go to use this camera in the field. The second issues was with getting the motion-sensor function working. It would trigger once and then not again. I played around with the settings and seemed to get it to work - but have no idea what actually fixed the issue.

The camera takes great photos - I've mainly been using it in the time-lapse mode (since I was having issues with the motion function). The photos are very clear and sharp. Daytime photos more so than night, but that's to be expected.

All-in-all I'm happy with the camera and look forward to using it this summer and the coming fall.

text_fidelity_a:
CRKT Halfachance Fixed Blade Parang Machete: 18 Inch Black Powder Coated Carbon Steel Parang Style Blade with Nylon Sheath for Survival, Hunting & Camping K920KKP Back in 1994 when I bought my waterfront property in Southwest Florida the first bid I got to (legally) trim my mangroves was $1,000.00. Even then I thought that the price was outrageous and I decided to do it myself. Needless to say it involves a lot of time and and some really good cutting tools (and skills). There's not a lot of room for maneuvering in the wetlands, the footing is hazardous, the flora and fauna always a challenge (most Florida plants either have thorns or some type of poison), and the bugs can drive you nuts. Now that I think about it, maybe the $1,000.00 would have been money well spent.

Now at age 67 the current bid for the same job is up to $8,000.00. Either the workers are a lot smarter or they don't really want to do this type of work. About 10 years ago I had some major surgery and had to hire three people to do the job for me. When I was watching them the youngest picked up and held a very pretty snake for his father to see, causing me to yell at his father to "put it down". I was really surprised to find out that they didn't know what a coral snake was. That hiring experience also resulted in all of my tools being damaged to the poiint of no return. But the real capper was that they cut the mangroves to a height of 4 feet -- when I had specified 6 feet. Fortunately no one reported me to the mangrove police.

So I have trimmed my own mangroves for 22 of the past 23 years, even at my advanced age. The secret is to keep your eyes and ears open, to use adequate insect repellant and sun protection, wear boots, long pants and long sleeves, and an SPF 50 hat. But the key to being able to trim mangroves for up to six hours at a time is to have a really good medium length machete. This CRKT Chanceinhell(CIH) really fits the bill. It has a durable, heavy and sharp blade, a well-constructed rubber grip for comfort, and a decent sheath that you can hang from your belt when you are using a different tool. This machete is blade heavy which gives you better balance for chopping versus slicing.

When I have the room to swing a machete, I rely on an Esee Lite machete (around $80.00), a blade perfect for slicing thicker wood. For the crowded areas where taking a full swing would be impossible (or foolhardy) I find chopping to be more efficient and safer. That is where the CIH hits the mark and is the best tool to use. You might wonder why I don't use a small chainsaw instead. There are a multitude of reasons: the high noise level masks other sounds that I need to be aware of ( like the movement of snakes, alligators and other critters), chainsaws are dangerous even when operating in the best of conditions (which is far from true in the wetlands), the probability of bounce-back or dropping a running chainsaw is pretty much guaranteed, and trucking in and out of the wetlands to refuel sets you up for additional problems.

So this year I'll be heading into the wetlands with my Chanceinhell and Esee, splitting my time between slicing and chopping, hoping to avoid any injuries. One thing that I can guarantee is that the experience is always interesting.
text_fidelity_b: CRKT Halfachance Fixed Blade Parang Machete: 18 Inch Black Powder Coated Carbon Steel Parang Style Blade with Nylon Sheath for Survival, Hunting & Camping K920KKP

text_fidelity_a:
WASING Outdoor Inflatable Lounger Nylon Fabric Beach Lounger Convenient Compression Air Bag Hangout Bean Bag Portable Dream Chair WS-InCOUCH-Blue I originally watched a viral video on facebook and saw that this type of lounger was available. I was curious about it. When this arrived in the mail, my husband immediately set it up and had me sit down in it. Instead of shaking it out (like you do with a garbage bag) he put it in front of a box fan and let it air up very quickly. Then you twist up the end and buckle it. It's extremely easy to use and light weight. It feels like a big balloon, but the material is a lot thicker.

When you sit on it, it feels like laying on a boat. It's soft, the air holds you up so you feel like you are floating. If you lay in the middle, go to reach for something, it will tilt back and fourth and feel like you are swaying on a boat in the water. My kids tried sitting on it and ended up sliding down inside it, so it's not really meant for little guys unless they sit on it like a chair or with someone. The more people on it however means the air escapes faster. If the air starts to escape after a while (an hour with one adult and two kids on it) then it is easy to fix that problem. Simply unbuckle the end, twist it a little tighter and re-buckle it. Then it's back to being nice and tight. When you are done it's easy to fold back down and put away.

This is such a neat idea for taking with you outdoors especially. It's rather long, my husband is around 6 1/2 feet tall and he can stretch out nicely on it. text_fidelity_a:
STEARNS Kids Puddle Jumper Deluxe Life Jacket We purchased five different life jackets for the 20 month old twins. The traditionally styled ones rode up at the shoulders. The Swimways Power Swimr System was difficult to get on and did nothing to keep the babies' heads above water. Nor did the Speedo UV 50.

We put the Stearns Kids Puddle Jumper on the first baby and she jumped into the pool for the first time in her life and paddled happily around for hours (see photo). The second twin took a little longer learning how to stay upright and she didn't want to take it off.

On plump babies, it's so tight in the arms that it is hard to get on and off. It's easier if you get both the jacket and their arms slick first (e.g, with sunscreen). However, neither twin complained once they got it on and there were no marks on their arms afterwards.

--------------------
5/12 Update. The twins are now three and can still wear their jackets although they take them off for swimming lessons. Their younger brother is a bit stouter and we have to grease up his chunky arms to get his on him. Another grandbaby on the way so I guess I need to buy a fourth one. The three jackets we have are also used by visiting kids so I realize that they are very tight on really stout kids and really loose on thin kids but, nonetheless, work well on most.

11/12 Update. The end of our third season and the three jackets are good as new. No wearing of the material and little fading despite having been left in the hot Georgia sun much of the time.

3/13 Update. The kids can all swim now but they still ask to have their water wings put on at time because they can just effortlessly float around. And, yes, they have already been swimming this year despite the 65 degree temperature of the pool right now.

7/13 Update. The fourth grandchild refused to wear the wings (or any life jacket). Fine with us since we are always with him and he's learning to swim. Love the new designs for this jacket. I need somebody else's baby to train now.

4/14 Update. Currently selling for $15 at Costco (fewer options)

12/14 Update. We still have the four jackets we purchased. All have faded a little but, otherwise, show no signs of their age.
text_fidelity_b: STEARNS Kids Puddle Jumper Deluxe Life Jacket

text_fidelity_a:
KUSIND Men Women Cowboy hat Cotton Trucker Hats Adjustable Baseball Cap Hat My wife has taken to wearing baseball caps (sometimes for bad hair days, sometimes to compliment her outfit), and so I keep an eye out for ones she'll like. She certainly doesn't have a collection to rival mine, but she likes ones that have a fun twist (image, saying). When I saw this KUSIND Men Women Cowboy hat Cotton Trucker Hats Adjustable Baseball Cap I asked and she jumped at it - apparently the saying is from the Harry Potter movies and along with that, she liked the sentiment.

We debated on the rating here: I felt it should get a 4 star, while she wanted 5, and since she's wearing it, I went with hers. So... why?

The hat looks nice: the dark gray has a washed out kind of look, that makes it looks "aged," but in that cool way. The hat is made of good materials. I'm pretty opinionated on what I look for in the quality of a hat and this one is decent, but it's where the first of my two "cons" comes in. For me I am not thrilled with that front connection between the cloth of the hat and the brim. As you note in the last two pictures, the stitching together is not consistent or as I feel it should be - tight against the brim. One side is better done than the other. The other thing we both noticed was the printing of the words: it's nice to look at and as long as it lasts, it's great. But we both worry this printing is likely to show wear and tear - though how quickly is yet to be seen. It is done decently, but having hats with printing rather than embroidery, I've seen them begin to peal.

The hat does adjust easily and well. My head is most certainly larger than hers, so I tried it on and it was great (for larger heads), then I adjusted it down for her and it fits perfectly. She loves it - and she looks great in it. I wish the pictures of her wearing it turned out better so you can see how great it looks on - but that coloring in the other images - the dark washed gray - is excellent. And once on it looks nice. Yes, I am still not thrilled with the inconsistent stitching of the top to brim - I think you can see what I'm talking about clearly in those images - but my wife likes it on and that's all that matters to me. text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-203 Pedometer with Activity Tracker The Omron is quiet small and light. I can have it in a pocket along with my wallet or iPhone and I don't notice it's there. But I'm skeptical about its accuracy.

I took a few walks and compared the distance it recorded with the route mapped out as a walk in Google Maps. The Omron would typically under measure my distance anywhere from 30 to 60 percent. I re-checked the height, weight and stride settings but that had no effect. I guess it's unrealistic that a pedometer can accurately measure distance.

A more serious flaw is that the unit does not keep lifetime stats -- it's memory is only 7 days. If you have a workout schedule where you need to keep a log of your daily steps, the 7 day memory feature is quite nice for when you forget to write down a day's results, but I would think most people would like to know how many steps they've taken after a year.

While I suppose the distance issue is forgivable -- most people buy a pedometer to keep track of steps, not miles traveled -- the lack of lifetime memory makes it hard to recommend this unit.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-203 Pedometer with Activity Tracker
